children.author: mips_avatar
children.text: You'd probably end up spending more on pcie h200s.  They're not that much cheaper than 8x sxm nodes and they only have 4 way nvlink. At the scale these guys were training at you'd probably want at a minimum an 8x nvlinked node for the trainer, even though you could technically fit the full training and optimizer states on a 4x h200 node.

FWIW that is about $331,000 on low-onboarding-grief clouds (e.g. vast.ai) right now using the SXM variants they used.

You might be able to shave that down using a different flavor of H200 (like PCIe) but it would take more hours, so benefits are unclear.

I keep a couple of older models (and much larger ones as well) for when I want to do stuff that is unrelated to computer programming because the models that are really good at that tend to fare less well at other stuff. Yes, I've seen that, but I wonder what is missing because I find it hard to believe that you can just do some RL and then end up with a model that is better across the board. I would find it far more believable if you outperformed on the benchmark that was your goal (assuming you selected training data to give you an edge there) and underperformed on things that you were not optimizing for. But since it all moves in one direction (better) I feel there must be some kind of unknown at play here. Even so, task specific AI is definitely the future, you don't hire a plumber to do your bookkeeping either...

Good point! First of all, none of the benchmark tasks were used in training, though the training data was designed to improve capabilities on tasks like TB4.1. If you consider TB4.1 the main target, the blog actually shows before/after results on several other benchmarks, with no regressions and even some improvements.

I always wonder what you lose when you start maxing out some specific benchmark. It is really hard to do this in a balanced way and I would love if everybody that did these kind of efforts would take the time to also list the before/afters of a number of other benchmarks that they did not use in their training.
